L2t: Under Free Exercise doctrine, a law that is neutral and generally applicable is generally not subject to strict scrutiny even if it burdens religious practice.
L3t: The amendment denies benefits to anyone who refuses reasonable medical care for any non-risk reason, so it does not target religion and only needs to be a reasonable limit on a benefit.
L4t: The court will likely uphold the amendment because it is religion-neutral, applying to all refusals of care, and is a reasonable limit on awarding death benefits.
L2f: The Supreme Court has held that any government benefit program touching religious conduct must be reviewed under the same standard as direct criminal prohibitions.
L3f: Because the amendment only sets a condition on receiving a government benefit and does not punish the officer's conduct, it raises no Free Exercise problem at all.
L4f: The court will likely uphold the amendment because it merely conditions a government benefit and does not penalize any individual's conduct.
